output:
**To Lee**

We’ve known each other 15 years, so I’ll keep this straight: I reckon it’s worth buying a dumper together rather than hiring one every time.

We hired the tracked dumper for 14 days this year. At £85 a day plus £30 delivery each time, that’s roughly £1,600 all in. There’s a 2019 500kg tracked one for sale in Faversham at £1,650 ono, and the seller says it had new tracks fitted last spring. If we get it for asking, that’s £825 each.

We’ve already got three patio digs and the Boughton drive booked for spring. At this year’s use, it could pay for itself in about a year; even at half that use, roughly two years — before servicing and repairs, obviously. It should hold its value too, so if it doesn’t work out, we can sell it on.

It’s not just the hire bill. In September, the hire place had no dumper, so we barrowed six tonnes of muck at Hernhill. That added two days, and your back was gone for a week. Another time, the delivery driver turned up at 11 and we lost half the morning. Having our own means we’re not relying on the hire place when we’ve got a job on.

I can keep it covered in my lean-to at the yard. For running costs, I suggest we split servicing 50/50, and whoever breaks it pays for the repair. We can agree how we handle any other costs when they come up.

Come and have a look at it with me this Saturday before someone else snaps it up. No pressure to buy — we can check it over and decide together whether the numbers stack up.
